requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Confirmed appworker did not exist (cmd-f781d4ff600f455c), then created via useradd -m -s /bin/bash with uid=1001 (cmd-e0ec977c7eec492d). Account persisted across a subsequent reboot (cmd-30d37235518d4cf0).

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 8,192 open files (nofile)
requirements.summary: limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile 8192 (cmd-a9d00e1d62ed4d52), directly verified in a real login shell (su -l equivalent) returning ulimit -n = 8192 both before and after a reboot (cmd-56fdbd5389c94ea3, cmd-30d37235518d4cf0).

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 256 processes (nproc)
requirements.summary: Same config sets soft/hard nproc 256, verified via login-shell ulimit -u = 256 both pre- and post-restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and constraining its login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes — are directly satisfied with real login-shell ulimit verification, not just config inspection. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly: a healthy pre-restart baseline, a background reboot acknowledgement, a changed boot identity (8336c3a1... -> 7248c716...) corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the account and limits. No unnecessary mutations were found.
limitations: Evidence relies on the executor's own captured command outputs and the fixed lifecycle snapshots; no independent live inspection of node1 was possible.
Login-session limit verification used 'sudo su - appworker -c ulimit' rather than an interactive SSH login as appworker, though this is functionally equivalent for PAM limits.d enforcement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were all either read-only diagnostics (os-release/id checks, boot_id captures, post-restart verification) or state changes with a clear, direct link to the task: useradd for the account, writing the limits.d config file, and the mandatory reboot for the restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary, unbounded, or unreverted extraneous mutations were observed; the after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no new failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and dpkg package health unchanged relative to before_prepare (aside from the boot-id-tagged temp files that are an inherent artifact of the required reboot itself).
